complexity.correctness_reason: Inserting a word of the maximum permitted length (1000 characters) recurses one frame per character and exceeds CPython's default recursion limit of 1000, raising RecursionError.
complexity.notes: Each word[1:] slice copies the remaining string, so a length-L operation does O(L^2) character copying and holds O(L^2) of slices across the recursion stack; walking the node iteratively (or passing an index) restores the expected O(L) per operation. L = word length, T = total inserted characters. Child-dict keys come from the fixed 26-letter alphabet, so lookups stay O(1) even in the worst case. Stylistically prefer `word[0] not in self.children` over `not word[0] in self.children`, and the insert base case would read more cleanly as an if/else rather than two consecutive `if word:` guards.
complexity.summary: A recursive trie: each node holds a dict of single-character children and a present flag, and insert/search/startsWith consume one character per recursive call, recursing on word[1:].
